### 2026-10-06 – Figured out what i need to figure out

**3h**

Figured out what i need to figure out
In this session i figured out what i needed to learn in order to make a flight controller. One of the main things being what i needed to learn in order to understand the logic behind  how it works. This helped me realize the things i already know and concepts that i can immediatedly implement. Things sich as a PID loop for calculating angle or the output, the sensor-process-output cycle for the drone to operate. I also found out things that i wasnt very familiar with. THings like sensor fusion, flight dynamics and physics and the new chip I need to learn how to program. I plan to learn these things in the coming sessions and get a real prototype or a schematic out.

### 2026-10-11 – in the last few days, I spent around a total of 7 hours learning about flight controllers and the different concepts behind how drones maintain stability and control their movement. I started with the

**7h**

in the last few days, I spent around a total of 7 hours learning about flight controllers and the different concepts behind how drones maintain stability and control their movement. I started with the basics of control theory and gradually worked my way toward understanding the different axes of movement, including pitch, yaw, and throttle. I also spent time learning about PID control, how it uses feedback to correct errors, and how its proportional, integral, and derivative components work together to keep a system stable. To solidify my understanding, I wrote a technical explanation of PID control in layman's terms( link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/15qsIWHHsLXW35jFxxsz_cWQ6nE3_AibIL6ItvMdiK1o/edit?tab=t.0) using real-world analogies to make the concepts easier to understand and explain to others.

After building a better understanding of the theory, I researched drone flight controllers and the different components that connect to them, including sensors, motors, and other electronic components needed for flight control. I wanted to understand not just what each component does, but also how they work together as a complete system. After much thought, I decided to keep my initial design simple by using an ESP32-WROOM development board alongside an IMU as the foundation of my DIY drone's flight controller. This approach gives me a manageable starting point while allowing me to apply the control theory and embedded systems knowledge I have been learning. Overall, today's session helped me connect theoretical concepts to a practical engineering project and gave me a clearer direction for the next stage of development.
